transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Atlas VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Atlas SRE), Sofia Alvarez (Atlas CTO)

Summary (auto):
- Integration discovery focusing on SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to data residency and latency, but evaluating tradeoffs vs Hosted.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing/SLA docs, run throughput estimates, and schedule POC kickoff.

Topics:
- SDK usage patterns (Python/Node) and official client features
- LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors and example patterns
- Using a gateway or proxy for tenant routing and auth
- Rate limiting, quotas, and throttling behavior
- Observability hooks: token-level cost, per-route latency/cost, traces, and logs
- Private (VPC) vs Dedicated tradeoffs and KMS integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, i'm jordan from redwood. do you want to quick intros?
[00:08] Maya: yeah maya here, vp engineering at atlas analytics, we own the inference infra for our customer-facing features.
[00:13] Liam: liam, platform eng / sre, i'll be owning the networking and rate-limit parts.
[00:16] Sofia: sofia cto, joining for context.
[00:18] Priya: priya from redwood's solutions engineering team, i'll cover integration patterns and benchmarks.
[00:24] Jordan: awesome — high level today we want to understand your stack and where you see redwood fitting: hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, or private vpc/on-prem.
[00:33] Maya: our main constraints are latency under 200ms p95 for short chat flows, and strict data residency for a subset of european customers. also we have existing wrappers in python and node.
[00:42] Priya: got it. what does your current integration look like — direct calls to openai or internal proxies?
[00:49] Maya: right now it's a mix: some teams call openai via a central gateway, others use an internal llama infra for cheaper offline batches. for real time product features we currently proxy through our api gateway which adds 30-40ms.
[01:02] Jordan: ok so gateway latency's an important factor. question about SDKs — are you primarily using python? node? do you rely on langchain or lamaindex?
[01:12] Maya: majority python services, a few node frontends. and yes, product team uses langchain for chaining prompts and llamaindex for retrieval pipelines — although sometimes the connector bits are custom.
[01:23] Priya: we have first-class python and node clients. they support streaming, function/tool calling, and built-in retry/backoff. for langchain and llamaindex we provide example connectors; some of our customers use the langchain redwood llm wrapper, others plug into the http client.
[01:36] Liam: how tight are those connectors? like, do they support token-level streaming and metadata for retrieval? we've had trouble mapping traces across the chain.
[01:45] Priya: yes — our langchain wrapper preserves streaming tokens and exposes hooks for tracer propagation. small caveat: in some transcriptions the package name got mis-typed as longchain, but it's the same. we also emit per-request trace ids you can inject into your gateway headers.
[01:58] Sofia: and for lamaindex — is that llamaindex? we've heard both names.
[02:03] Priya: llamaindex, yep, sorry for the slur — sometimes auto-transcript reads llama as lama. our docs have exact snippets.
[02:10] Jordan: let's talk gateway/proxy models — do you plan to keep the existing gateway and route to redwood endpoints, or want redwood to sit behind your gateway forever?
[02:19] Maya: ideally we keep our gateway as the single ingress for auth/routing. we want to avoid clients talking directly to external endpoints.
[02:26] Priya: that's a very common pattern. customers use a gateway with short-lived tokens or a tenant proxy. we've seen two approaches: 1) gateway forwards requests to redwood hosted api with mTLS and a per-tenant header; 2) for Dedicated/Private, you host a small edge proxy in your VPC and route to the private redwood control plane. both supported.
[02:45] Liam: what about rate limits/quotas? we have spikes during batch jobs and a steady 4-6 rps baseline, peak 60 rps for some tenants.
[02:55] Priya: rate limits can be enforced at multiple layers — your gateway, our client SDKs (local token buckets), and server-side quotas per API key or per-tenant. for Hosted we have per-account quotas and adaptive throttling; Dedicated allows custom quota configs and higher throughput; Private gives you full control. we typically recommend token-bucket at gateway + server-side quotas.
[03:18] Maya: curious how you surface throttling in the SDK — consistent error codes? backoff headers?
[03:24] Priya: we return structured error codes and recommend an exponential backoff. SDKs expose the retry policy and surface headers like x-rw-quota-remaining and x-rw-retry-after. we also emit a throttling event to the observability hooks so you can alert.
[03:39] Jordan: let's cover observability — what telemetry do you expose?
[03:43] Priya: token-level cost per request, per-route p50/p95 latency, model version used, kernel/quantization profile, and per-request trace id. we push metrics to your metrics endpoint via statsd/prometheus push or you can pull via our dashboard api.
[03:58] Liam: do you support distributed tracing correlation? we use jaeger and open telemetry collector.
[04:03] Priya: yes, we attach traceparent headers and provide a trace id in response, and we have open-telemetry compatible spans you can ingest. some early customers pipe our events into their otel collector.
[04:14] Maya: for PII concerns, we need to know what is retained and for how long. do you have a data retention policy and KMS integration?
[04:22] Priya: Hosted keeps transient logs for 30 days by default; we have options for shorter retention. Dedicated and Private allow customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; Private can be completely air-gapped. we'll send the security pack (SOC 2, encryption, network diagram).
[04:36] Sofia: on latency — you mentioned optimizing kernels/quantization. what should we expect for our short chat flows (avg 512 tokens) on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:46] Priya: for 512 tokens, on equivalent GPU hardware Dedicated typically has lower tail latency because of reserved capacity and tuned batching. Hosted can be comparable but depends on noisy neighbors. we'll run a throughput estimate for your 5 rps baseline and expected peak so you can see p95 numbers.
[05:00] Liam: can we run a smoke POC — small dataset, run bench for 24 hours? we want to see real-world latency and cost.
[05:06] Jordan: absolutely — typical POC: 2-week pilot, we provide dedicated trial capacity or hosted trial with priority routing. for your needs, Dedicated trial might be better given latency targets and EU residency.
[05:20] Maya: what about integrations with langchain/llamaindex retrieval — can we point retrieval to our private vector store?
[05:26] Priya: yes — retrieval stays in your stack. our SDKs support streaming in retrieved docs metadata and embeddings. if you want private deployment, we can run inside your VPC with network-level access to your vector db so nothing leaves your network.
[05:40] Liam: any gotchas with rate-limiting when using batching / KV cache? we've had duplicate charges from batch retries.
[05:47] Priya: good point — batching reduces per-token cost but complicates retry semantics. our SDKs implement idempotency keys and k-v cache management; for critical workflows we recommend explicit idempotency and server-side dedupe. we'll add notes to the POC runbook.
[06:03] Sofia: i want to clarify security for Private — how does auth work? sso, service accounts, and kms?
[06:10] Priya: Private supports SAML SSO for console, service accounts with short-lived tokens for apps, and you can bring-your-own KMS (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM) for key material. audit logs stream to your SIEM.
[06:21] Maya: do you have example deployment manifests or terraform?
[06:25] Priya: yes we provide terraform modules and Helm charts for the private agent and edge proxies. we'll link the repo.
[06:32] Jordan: quick question on developer DX — do you support a hosted api key model and also SCIM provisioning for teams?
[06:38] Priya: hosted supports api keys, scim for users, and role-based access control. Dedicated adds SSO and more granular RBAC.
[06:46] Liam: curious about observability hooks for cost attribution — can we get token-level cost per team/route?
[06:51] Priya: we expose token-level cost and per-route breakdowns in the console and via an events api. you can tag requests with route or project metadata and we correlate billing.
[06:59] Maya: what is the typical turnaround to get a dedicated environment provisioned for a POC?
[07:05] Jordan: usually 48-72 hours for trial capacity if quotas allow; for Private there's an onboarding checklist and it can take a few days to a couple of weeks depending on networking approvals.
[07:15] Sofia: any regulatory concerns for EU data? like data residency in eu regions?
[07:19] Priya: we have EU-hosted regions, and Dedicated/Private can be pinned to region. for strict residency we recommend Private where control is fully yours.
[07:29] Maya: a couple of smaller integration questions: 1) does the node sdk support streaming over web sockets? 2) do you have examples for langchain retrieval plus function calling?
[07:38] Priya: node sdk supports http streaming and websockets for long-lived connections. and yes — we've published sample notebooks for langchain + retrieval + function calling.
[07:49] Liam: what about throttling backoff headers again — can we rely on them for autoscaling signals?
[07:54] Priya: yes you can. x-rw-quota-remaining and x-rw-retry-after are consistent; many customers use the quota_remaining metric to drive horizontal scaling in the gateway.
[08:06] Jordan: let's surface any blockers — what's preventing a quick POC?
[08:10] Maya: main blockers: 1) security review signoff, 2) budget approval for Dedicated trial if needed, 3) alignment on success metrics.
[08:19] Sofia: also we need a short runbook showing how to swap in redwood endpoints behind our gateway for canary traffic.
[08:25] Priya: we'll include a canary runbook and a sample nginx proxy snippet.
[08:30] Jordan: i'll send pricing and SLA and the security pack. priya will run benchmarks.
[08:34] Maya: sounds good.

[38:34] Jordan: quick recap — we'll send pricing, security docs, terraform/helm snippets, and a benchmark sheet. schedule POC kickoff after maya shares prompts and infra availability.
[38:46] Priya: action items recorded — i'll run the throughput estimates and include expected p95 numbers for hosted vs dedicated, plus a recommended batch / kv cache configuration.
[38:58] Maya: ok thanks all, we'll follow up in crm.
[39:02] Sofia: thanks, talk soon.
